_comment: Payload budget for the published npm tarball (road-to-zero-ceremony-install Phase 4). MEASURED, NEVER INVENTED — the numbers below come from `npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts` on the tracked tree at 9.9.0 (2026-07-31). Two metrics, both genuinely ungated before this file: COMPRESSED tarball size, and PER-SKILL share of the skills subtree. The UNPACKED size is deliberately absent — it is already owned by src/config/evaluator-budgets.json (unpacked_size_mb), and a second number for one lever is how three conflicting figures start circulating.
measurement_conditions: npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts, run at the repo root on a clean checkout. `--ignore-scripts` means NO build runs, so dist/cli, dist/ui, dist/mcp and dist/hooks are absent and the figure covers only the TRACKED payload (src/scripts/, dist/agent-src/, dist/install/, docs/guidelines/, templates). That is deliberate: this gate is always-on for every PR, and the tracked content tree is exactly the surface that grows by accretion. The built artifact is ~5.4 MB larger and is gated separately, at release time, by evaluator-budgets.unpacked_size_mb.

packed_size_mb.baseline_note_2026_08_23: 8.4 → 9.2 re-baselined 2026-08-23. RATCHET RESET, not the config bent around a failing check: the cap was exhausted at TRUNK level before the tripping branch existed. MEASURED on clean clones under the documented conditions — origin/main at f16c7d9df reads 8.3911, i.e. 8.9 KB under its own cap; PR #1597 reads 8.4083 local / 8.416 CI, +17.2 KB across 4 new pack entries of functional source its roadmap deliberately adds. With 8.9 KB of headroom ANY commit reds this gate, which is the failure the 2026-08-20 note predicted in writing, arriving a second time three days later. Max = 8.4083 × 1.095, derived from this file's own regression_pct: 10 rather than from the tripping measurement; last_measured records CI's 8.416, the enforcing environment and the higher of the disagreeing pair. GIVEN UP: ~0.79 MB of unpoliced accretion — this gate catches a step change in payload, which regression_pct still catches at any cap, and it cannot police 17 KB increments. REJECTED, measured rather than argued: payload reduction inside the PR — the whitelist is already tight (docs/guidelines/ plus three named contracts), tests/ is 6 KB and agents/ 39 KB uncompressed, so excluding both saves ~13 KB compressed and does not clear even this one PR. The structural surface the 2026-08-20 note named (src/scripts/ at 14.9 MB unpacked, src/agent-src/ duplicating dist/agent-src/) is still unexamined and still the open debt this raise defers. Revisit-if: a single PR moves the figure by more than regression_pct, or the drain ends and the cap can ratchet DOWN from a re-measured trunk — never up again from a fresh trip. DECIDED BY: maintainer, numbered-options option 1, after the alternative above was measured and the exhaustion was reported rather than the cap raised silently.
packed_size_mb.method: npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts → dist.size / 1e6 (the compressed tarball a consumer actually downloads)
packed_size_mb.baseline_note_2026_08_24: 8.4 → 9.1 re-baselined 2026-08-24, and this is a RATCHET RESET rather than the config bent around a failing check. The discriminator this file demands, answered with a measurement rather than an argument: THE TRUNK WAS ALREADY AT THE CEILING BEFORE THE CHANGE THAT TRIPPED IT EXISTED. `origin/main` at f16c7d9df measures 8.3911 under the documented conditions — 8.9 KB of headroom against an 8.4 cap, i.e. 0.1 %. An addition of any size crosses it. That is verbatim the failure mode the 2026-08-20 note predicted in writing — 'a cap pinned just above the measurement reds on the next commit and teaches the reader to raise it again' — arriving on schedule for the SECOND time, which is why the correction here is the headroom and not the payload. TRIP CAUSE: merging `origin/main` into `drain/chained-clip-continuity` (PR #1598). The branch adds ~2,600 net lines inside packed paths — `src/scripts/lint_adapter_tier.ts` (662 lines; it is the gate that verifies the generated tier table in `docs/contracts/provider-lifecycle.md`, so it must ship), the ai-video adapter / seam-plan / stitch shell libraries, and the `model-capabilities/*.json` files read at runtime — landing 39 KB over the cap. NEITHER SIDE WAS OVER ALONE; together they cross, which is the shape a merge produces and no per-branch check can see. MEASURED, on two clean detached worktrees with unbuilt `dist/` per `measurement_conditions` (so dist/cli, dist/ui, dist/mcp and dist/hooks absent): main 8.3911 (2,746 entries) · branch 8.4305 (2,753 entries) · CI 8.439 (Consistency job 97266868959). `last_measured` records CI's 8.439 — the enforcing environment and the higher of the disagreeing pair, per the rule the 2026-08-10 and 2026-08-20 notes both applied to their own; the ~8 KB CI-over-local gap matches the pattern both recorded. The 10 % regression rule did NOT trip (threshold 8.586 against the prior `last_measured` 7.805); only the absolute cap did. Max set to 9.1, ~7.8 % headroom over 8.439, which is the ~8 % the 5.903/6.4, 7.238/7.8 and 7.805/8.4 pairs all carried: deliberately not a number that merely clears. ALTERNATIVE EXAMINED AND NOT TAKEN, measured rather than argued, and its verdict left HONESTLY OPEN: excluding `src/scripts/ai_council/` — the tree the 2026-08-20 note names as the one whose consumer need is 'unverified', 0.903 MB as measured here — saves 270 KB compressed (8.4305 → 8.1607, under the OLD cap with 239 KB to spare). It is not taken here because whether it is SAFE is still undecided, and this note deliberately does not decide it. `src/server/routes/wizard.ts:48` imports `apiOnQuotaView` from `scripts/ai_council/transport_resolver.js`, and `council:status` is a registered verb in `src/cli/registry.ts` — but the specifier ends in `.js` and therefore cannot settle whether it resolves to the TS source under `src/scripts/` or to built output under `dist/` in a published install. An earlier draft of this note asserted that the exclusion 'breaks the wizard quota view in every consumer install'; that was an over-claim read off the specifier, and it is retracted here rather than quietly dropped. What IS established: `src/cli/python/workspace_hosts.ts:180-191` records a real `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in a global install caused by a shipped module importing from a directory absent from `files[]`, and `src/server/routes/wizard.ts:136-137` invokes `bash src/scripts/install_anthropic_key.sh` BY PATH at runtime. So a blanket trim of `src/scripts/` is unsafe, while the ai_council-specific verdict needs a global-install smoke test rather than a reading of an import. THE DEBT IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN, which is the one thing the 2026-08-20 note promised and did not deliver: it said 'this raise buys the time to write one [a roadmap]', and no roadmap was ever written — a grep of `agents/roadmaps/` (active, `stubs/`, `later/`, `archive/`) finds no payload-reduction plan. `agents/roadmaps/archive/road-to-npm-payload-reduction.md` lands in this same change and carries the measured split: `src/scripts/` is 16.384 MB of the 28.604 MB unpacked payload (57.3 %, 1,158 files) and is the actual growth surface; `dist/agent-src/` is 8.040 MB; `src/agent-src/` is 1.347 MB and partly duplicates it, unmeasured until that roadmap's Phase 1.3. Its Phase 2.3 lowers this cap again, so `max: 9.1` still standing later is the visible signal the plan did not finish. [AMENDED 2026-08-24 by the run that finished it, because that sentence would otherwise mislead in the opposite direction: the plan DID finish, and 9.1 is now its RESULT rather than its deferral signal — see baseline_note_2026_08_24_lowered. The roadmap path in this sentence was rewritten from agents/roadmaps/ to agents/roadmaps/archive/ by the archival ref-migration, so a dated note now points at a path that did not exist on its own date; the migration is kept because the reference must resolve, and it is flagged here rather than left to read as if the file had always been archived.] A raise that defers the same debt a fourth time with no plan is a formality, so this one carries the plan. DECIDED BY: maintainer, on the PR that tripped it, chosen from numbered options carrying the measurements above rather than applied to make a red go away — and the write itself was performed by the maintainer, because the block-config-weakening guard refused four agent attempts at this file. That is the standing this file's `owner: maintainer` requires, enforced rather than asserted. MET A SECOND, INDEPENDENT RESET IN A MERGE, 2026-08-24: the drain's council-evidence-integrity branch reached the same diagnosis from the same measurement (main at 8.3911, 8.9 KB of headroom) and set 9.2 instead of 9.1, landing on trunk first. The HIGHER cap prevails and BOTH derivations are kept, because two independent readings converging on one trip cause is the strongest evidence this entry has ever carried — and dropping one of them would leave the record looking like a single unreviewed judgement. `last_measured` is re-measured on the merged tree rather than taken from either side, per the method every prior entry here prescribes.
packed_size_mb.baseline_note_2026_08_20: 7.8 → 8.4 re-baselined 2026-08-20, and this is a RATCHET RESET rather than the config bent around a failing check — the discriminator the 2026-08-10 note demands, answered here. TRIP CAUSE: nothing was added. `origin/main` at cfd8426d9 measures 7.7916 under the documented conditions, and CI reads ~7 KB above the local figure, so trunk itself already stood ~8 KB below a 7.8 cap before the release branch existed; the 14.6.0 CHANGELOG entry (6.3 KB — a file on the release-PR shape allowlist, i.e. the release's own permitted payload) is what crossed it, at 7.7979 local / 7.805 CI. That is precisely the failure mode the 2026-08-10 note predicted in writing — 'a cap pinned just above the measurement reds on the next commit and teaches the reader to raise it again' — arriving on schedule, which is why the correction here is the headroom and not the payload. MEASURED, on a clean clone of each tree with the method `measurement_conditions` documents (unbuilt dist/, so dist/cli, dist/ui, dist/mcp and dist/hooks absent): main 7.7916 · release/14.6.0 7.7979 · CI 7.805 (Consistency job 96239721013). `last_measured` records CI's 7.805 — the enforcing environment and the higher of the disagreeing pair, per the same rule the 2026-08-10 note applied to its own. Max set to 8.4, ~7.6 % headroom over 7.805, which is the ~8 % both the 5.903/6.4 and 7.238/7.8 pairs carried: deliberately not a number that merely clears. ALTERNATIVE EXAMINED AND REJECTED, measured rather than argued: forcing the CHANGELOG era split early — the one payload reduction that IS on the release-PR allowlist, so it could have landed without touching main at all — moves the 144-line 14.5.0 section (7,266 bytes) into `docs/archive/`, which sits outside `files[]`. It saves 1.0 KB compressed (7.7979 → 7.7969). Prose compresses; a ~7 KB deficit cannot be closed by relocating 7 KB of prose. Recorded so it is not re-proposed as the cheap fix it looks like. NOT EXAMINED HERE, and named as the open question this raise defers rather than answers: `src/scripts/` is 14.9 MB of the 26.0 MB unpacked payload and is the actual growth surface, `src/agent-src/` partly duplicates `dist/agent-src/`, and whether a consumer needs the 846 KB `src/scripts/ai_council/` tree at all is unverified. Each is a structural change with its own blast radius, not a release-time edit — that belongs in a roadmap, and this raise buys the time to write one. A debt this note records, not one it discharges. DECIDED BY: maintainer, on the release that tripped it, in its own PR against main — `src/config/pack-size-budget.json` is not on the release-PR shape allowlist, so this cannot ride the release branch and is not smuggled into one.
packed_size_mb.baseline_note_2026_08_10: 6.9 → 7.8 re-baselined 2026-08-10. WHICH OF THE TWO THIS IS, stated because the guard asks: a RATCHET RESET, not the config bent around a failing check — and the discriminator is that the payload is real and needed rather than that the check was inconvenient. The 44 KB is two source files a shipped instruction depends on, the cheaper alternative was examined and rejected on that ground (below), the new cap carries ~8% headroom over the higher of two disagreeing measurements rather than clearing by a hair, and the raise was put to the maintainer as a decision instead of applied to make a red go away. A reader who disagrees has everything needed to reverse it: the measurement, its method, the trip cause, and the rejected option. Maintainer-decided in the PR that tripped it, surfaced rather than smuggled — the same standing this file's `owner: maintainer` requires. MEASURED TWICE, and the two do not agree: CI reported 6.907 on this exact commit, a local run under the documented conditions reports 7.238. The 331 KB gap is UNEXPLAINED — the tree matches the pushed commit and only this file differs — so the cap is set over the HIGHER figure rather than the convenient one, and the discrepancy is recorded here as an open question instead of resolved by assumption. A third party reproducing this should expect either number and should not treat the lower one as authoritative. Separately, and this part IS understood: `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts` in a worktree that has been BUILT reads 8.45, because the flag assumes dist/cli, dist/ui, dist/mcp and dist/hooks are absent and a built tree has them. That figure is not comparable to this budget and must never be written here — recorded because it is a trap the documented method invites. Trip cause: road-to-conformance-round5 Phase 3 added src/scripts/hooks/turn_end_gate_hook.ts (32 KB) and src/scripts/measure_turn_end_gate.ts (12 KB) in packed paths plus schema/template/contract growth, landing 7 KB over a 6.9 cap. Max set to 7.8 (~8% headroom over 7.238, and ~13% over CI's 6.907) for the reason the 2026-08-05 note already gives: a cap pinned just above the measurement reds on the next commit and teaches the reader to raise it again. ALTERNATIVE EXAMINED AND REJECTED, so it is not re-proposed: dropping measure_turn_end_gate.ts from the pack would have cleared the cap with room, but the settings description added in the same change instructs CONSUMERS to run that script against their own transcript store before arming the gate — excluding it would break a shipped instruction.
packed_size_mb.baseline_note: 5.903 → 6.398 re-baselined 2026-08-05. This is a RE-BASELINE, not a carve-out for the change that tripped it: measured on the tracked tree, `origin/main` alone was already at 6.372 of a 6.4 cap, so 28 KB of headroom remained after months of accretion and the next legitimate addition of any size was going to cross it. The addition here is 26 KB — docs/contracts/settings-classes.md (the A/B/C fence, read at RUNTIME by the settings writer, so it must ship) plus src/server/io/yamlIO.ts (imported by that writer to preserve the user's comments). CI measures ~4 KB above the local figure because it regenerates dist/agent-src first. Max set to 6.9 rather than to a number that merely clears: a cap pinned 2 KB above the measurement reds on the next commit and teaches the reader to raise it again, which is how a budget becomes a formality. That restores the ~8% headroom the 5.903/6.4 pair originally carried. The `owner: maintainer` on this file stands — this raise is surfaced in the PR for that decision, not smuggled.
packed_size_mb.baseline_note_2026_08_24_lowered: 9.2 -> 9.1 LOWERED 2026-08-24 — the first DOWNWARD move in this file's history, and the reason it is possible is that road-to-npm-payload-reduction measured the lever the previous four raises kept deferring. Method, because the verdicts turn on it: a behavioural global-install harness (src/scripts/pack_install_smoke.ts) packs a real BUILT tarball, installs it into a throwaway prefix, and runs eleven consumer probes including the bash orchestrator FROM the installed tree, which is the only probe that exercises path-reachability rather than imports. Sensitivity was proven by sabotage before any verdict was trusted: excluding src/scripts/_lib/ produces ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on four probes. WHAT THE BISECT FOUND, and it retires a suggestion this file has carried since 2026-08-20: EVERY named subtree SHIPS. src/scripts/ai_council/ — the 270 KB candidate the 2026-08-24 note left explicitly undecided — breaks council:status AND hooks:status with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. So does src/scripts/hooks/ (271.5 KB), src/scripts/_cli/ (204.1 KB), src/agent-src/ (101.8 KB), src/scripts/ai-video/ (95.4 KB, its shell entry point), src/scripts/mcp_server/ (53.1 KB). Two of those first read GREEN and flipped RED when the probe set was widened with mcp:setup and an ai-video shell check — recorded because it is the exact false-negative shape this file's own Risk 2 names, caught rather than shipped. WHAT IS ACTUALLY REMOVABLE is three FILE PATTERNS, not subtrees, and no prior note looked for them: dist/**/*.map (323.5 KB), dist/agent-src/skills/**/evals/** (56.2 KB), src/**/*.test.ts + *.spec.ts (22.6 KB) — 402.9 KB on the built tarball, all eleven probes green together. MEASURED under this file's own documented conditions (npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts, clean unbuilt worktree, which is what check_pack_size reads): 8.5596 -> 8.4667 MB, 2,775 -> 2,609 entries, a 92.9 KB drop. The gap between 402.9 KB and 92.9 KB is not a discrepancy: most of the .map saving lives in dist/cli, dist/ui, dist/mcp and dist/hooks, which --ignore-scripts excludes by design. HEADROOM IS 7.4 %, NOT 8 %, and the number is stated exactly rather than rounded up to match the pattern: 9.1 over the CI-adjusted 8.475 (local 8.4667 plus the ~8 KB CI delta every prior note here records) is 7.37 %. The 5.903/6.4, 7.238/7.8, 7.805/8.4 and 8.439/9.1 pairs carried ~8 %; this one carries slightly less, which is a real if small increase in flake risk and is why the falsifier below names it. STILL OPEN, quantified for the first time: src/agent-src/ is 94.2 % byte-identical to dist/agent-src/ (284 of 297 files, 2,144,870 of 2,276,707 bytes, content-hash diff). Two prior notes called this 'partial'; it is near-total. It is NOT removable by exclusion — nine shipped scripts under src/scripts/ import through it (build_archive_index, check_estate_count, eval_ui_triviality, explain_run, lint_ui_stack_bundles, skill_usage_report, smoke_quickstart, telemetry_disclosure_hook, utilization_report) while dist/agent-src/ is the tree the installer deploys, so the two copies ship for different reasons. Repointing those imports at dist/ would make source depend on a generated projection, which src/rules/source-of-truth.md exists to prevent. AI council 2026-08-24, 2/2: that needs an ADR covering compiled script entry points and asset resolution, not another files[] experiment. Worth ~102 KB and deliberately not taken here. TRADE-OFF ACCEPTED, named rather than absorbed: excluding dist/**/*.map means published packages carry no source maps, so consumer stack traces show compiled names. GREEN here means 'no regression across the recorded eleven-probe matrix', never 'semantically equivalent'. REVISIT-IF: three clean CI runs measure above 9.1 (the method does not match the gate); or observed run-to-run variance exceeds the 7.4 % margin, making the ratchet noise rather than a floor; or the src/agent-src/ ADR lands and the cap can drop again. NEVER raise it again from a fresh trip without the discriminator the 2026-08-10 note demands. DECIDED BY: AI council 2026-08-24, 2/2 convergent (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 + openai/codex-default, 2 rounds, blind peer review), on a maintainer delegation of owner-reserved blockers for an autonomous drain run. Both seats independently required the 7.4 % to be stated exactly and the GREEN to be scoped to the probe matrix.

per_skill_share.basis: a single skill's share of the total bytes under dist/agent-src/skills/ in the tarball
per_skill_share.rationale: Measured 2026-07-31: the largest non-excepted skill is corpus-grounding at 2.33%, so a 5% cap is green with better than 2x headroom and red for any skill that doubles. It is a falsifiable gate, not a ritual one.

design-intelligence.reason: 771 KB of BM25 corpus (27 CSVs + 16 design-language prose specs + manifest.json) consumed at runtime by corpus-grounding's retriever, and referenced by 6 further skills. Moving it behind a lazy fetch would add a network dependency to a skill that works offline today — the same trade-off ADR-061 §8 already REJECTED for a 745 KB font index. The exception is visible debt, not an endorsement: raising max_pct requires a reason in the same commit.
design-intelligence.baseline_note_2026_08_13: 23.0 → 23.5 on 2026-08-13, and the reason belongs in this file per the sentence above. WHAT WAS ADOPTED: data/motion.csv, 10.5 KB, 16 rows. WHY IT IS NOT DISCRETIONARY: the roadmap's three design dials were all in its original scope, and two of the three (variance, density) were already portable — variance's keywords resolve against the local styles.csv (2/3/3 hits) and density is three pure range maps. The motion dial is not: upstream filters its corpus rows by `Intensity Tier == <dial tier>`, and that column exists only in motion.csv, so shipping the dial without the file means shipping a flag that silently does nothing. Two of three dials plus an inert third is a worse surface than three working ones. WHAT WAS DECLINED IN THE SAME PASS, so this is not a ratchet slipping: google-fonts.csv (743 KB — ADR-061 §8 rejects it by name and by size; the 2026-06-16 amendment authorises a slim top-N slice from a different mirror, not this file), typography.csv (our curated font-pairings-reference.csv is the ADR's working substitution), six desktop-UI stacks outside frontend-design's scope, and eleven content-drifted files nobody has reviewed. The base pin in ATTRIBUTION.md is deliberately NOT bumped for the same reason. HONEST LIMIT ON THE NUMBER: 22.63 is the committed measurement, not a fresh one — check_pack_size cannot be re-measured from a built worktree (it reads 9.096 against the 7.8 packed cap before any change, the trap the packed_size_mb note above documents), so the post-adoption share is arithmetic (~22.87 %) and the new cap carries ~0.6 pp over it rather than clearing by a hair. DECIDED BY: AI council, 2026-08-13, on a maintainer delegation — and honestly, by ONE member over two rounds, not by convergence: the second seat returned exit_1 (the codex CLI refuses a git worktree as an untrusted directory). Recorded as a single-member review in agents/evidence/analysis/design-system-blockers-council.md.
